author: elena_rostova
title: ADR 0001: Migrate from Legacy Braintree to Stripe Payment Intents API
body:
Status: accepted

Context:
Legacy Braintree integration does not support European 3D Secure 2 authentication and suffers from elevated drop-off during checkout.

Decision:
Migrate checkout payment processing to Stripe Payment Intents with asynchronous webhook settlement.

Consequences:
- Full 3DS2 compliance.
- Checkout authorization latency reduced to <800ms.
- Requires webhook listener for asynchronous capture.

author: david_kim
title: Issue #8: Stripe API 429 Rate Limits encountered during flash sale traffic
body: During peak traffic burst, worker threads made simultaneous calls to Stripe charges API exceeding the 100 req/sec rate limit without jittered exponential backoff.

author: marcus_vance
title: PR #14: Implement Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter for Stripe API (Closes #8)
body: Adds decorator with decorator-level exponential backoff with full jitter (Decorrelated Jitter algorithm). Retries up to 4 times before failing.

author: sarah_chen
title: Review on PR #14: Reject fixed interval retries
body: Fixed 500ms sleep will create thundering herd when Stripe recovers. We must reject fixed sleep in favor of exponential backoff with randomized full jitter.

author: elena_rostova
title: ADR 0002: Use Redis Distributed Lock and Idempotency Key for Webhooks
body:
Status: accepted

Context:
Stripe webhook delivery guarantees at-least-once delivery. Duplicate payment.succeeded events caused double order fulfillment.

Decision:
Store processed Stripe event_ids in Redis with a 24-hour TTL and acquire a distributed mutex lock before processing webhook payloads.

Consequences:
- Zero duplicate order fulfillments.
- Redis availability required for payment reconciliation.

author: elena_rostova
title: feat(database): migrate to SQLAlchemy async connection pool with PgBouncer
body: Replaces raw psycopg2 connection per request with async connection pool. Reduces connection pool exhaustion under 2,000 checkout req/sec.

author: david_kim
title: Issue #5: Duplicate customer charges under concurrent checkout clicks
body: Impatient users double clicking Pay Now sent parallel requests to /checkout initiating two distinct payment authorization transactions.

author: sarah_chen
title: PR #18: Idempotency-Key Header Middleware with SHA-256 Request Hashing (Closes #5)
body: Introduces Idempotency-Key HTTP header middleware computing SHA-256 digest of payload. Cache hit returns cached HTTP response immediately.

author: elena_rostova
title: Review on PR #18: Reject database-level transaction locks for idempotency
body: Using row-level database locks (SELECT FOR UPDATE) on the checkout table creates bottleneck deadlock risks during sales. Redis key-value atomicity is required.

author: marcus_vance
title: ADR 0003: Webhook-First Asynchronous Order Confirmation
body:
Status: accepted

Context:
Sync browser checkout redirect was dropping orders when mobile users closed Safari before the success return page loaded.

Decision:
Treat Stripe payment_intent.succeeded webhook event as the single source of truth for confirming orders rather than client-side redirects.

Consequences:
- Zero lost orders from closed tabs.
- Frontend displays pending state and listens via WebSocket.

author: sarah_chen
title: PR #22: Webhook signature verification with HMAC-SHA256 and replay tolerance
body: Validates Stripe-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 secret key and enforces a 300-second maximum timestamp drift window to prevent replay attacks.

author: elena_rostova
title: Review on PR #22: Reject skipping signature verification in development
body: Bypassing webhook signature checks via a debug flag risks shipping unverified endpoints to production. Verification must run in all environments with test keys.

author: david_kim
title: ADR 0004: Support Partial Refunds with Line-Item Reversal Ledger
body:
Status: accepted

Context:
Customers returning one item out of a multi-item purchase required customer support intervention because the system only supported full-order voiding.

Decision:
Implement immutable append-only line-item reversal records tracking fractional refunds against order authorization totals.

Consequences:
- Eliminates manual support overrides for returns.
- Prevents cumulative refunds from exceeding original captured amount.

author: marcus_vance
title: Issue #11: Floating point rounding discrepancies during multi-currency partial refunds
body: Using standard IEEE 754 float types caused a 1-cent mismatch ($19.99 vs $19.989999) between partial refund sum and total charge.

author: sarah_chen
title: PR #29: Migrate refund math to integer cents and Decimal representation (Closes #11)
body: Converts all monetary fields to 64-bit integer minor currency units (cents) and Python Decimal to prevent floating point inaccuracies.

author: elena_rostova
title: Review on PR #29: Reject client-supplied refund timestamps
body: Relying on client timestamps allows fraudulent out-of-order refund attempts. Timestamps must strictly be generated by server UTC monotonic clock.

author: david_kim
title: Issue #19: Toxic malformed webhook payloads causing infinite queue retry loops
body: Unparseable webhook payload triggered an unhandled exception causing RabbitMQ consumer to continually NACK and requeue, stalling normal processing.

author: marcus_vance
title: PR #35: Route unparseable webhook messages to Dead Letter Queue after 3 failed deliveries (Closes #19)
body: Configures DLQ with max-retries=3. Stalls are avoided by parking invalid messages for engineer inspection without blocking main line.

author: sarah_chen
title: ADR 0005: Dual-token vault encryption for PCI-DSS compliance
body:
Status: accepted

Context:
PCI-DSS Scope Level 1 audit requires payment card numbers to never enter merchant application server memory or disk storage.

Decision:
Use Stripe Elements tokenization directly in client browser, receiving only opaque payment_method_id tokens on payment-core backend.

Consequences:
- Achieves PCI SAQ A eligibility, drastically reducing compliance overhead.
- Eliminates need for custom HSM or PAN storage on premises.

author: elena_rostova
title: Review on PR #38: Reject caching unencrypted CVV in memory
body: Storing raw CVVs even temporarily in Redis or local process memory is a direct violation of PCI-DSS requirement 3.2. Prohibit all CVV persistence.
